The world’s population is continuing to become more urbanized, particularly in low and middle-income countries located in the global South. During the 21st century, urbanization rates in Africa have increased considerably as rapidly growing populations have migrated to cities for economic opportunities. Although research has tended to focus on the largest “megacities”, there are also many rapidly growing secondary cities that are smaller in size but more numerous. The EcoGRAPH group is using satellite remote sensing to map historical patterns of urban growth in Africa and India. These data will be used to parameterize spatially explicit urban growth models for making future projections of urban expansion ([Korah et al. 2024](#expansion-refs)). These projections will provide a basis for assessing how expanding cities will interact with the changing climate to influence human exposure to heat and infectious diseases.

To map regional patterns of urban expansion in West Africa, we developed novel technique that more accurately capture the growth of smaller secondary cities than global land cover products ([Korah and Wimberly, 2024b](#expansion-refs)). Using twenty years of historical data, we showed that secondary cities were growing faster than larger primary cities, exhibiting more sprawing growth, and accounting for an increasing proportion of the total developed land cover ([Korah and Wimberly, 2024a](#expansion-refs)). A mixed methods study conducted in Ghana found that secondary cities had lower land and rent costs and more diverse land allocations than primary cities, creating more opportunities for developers as well as individuals seeking housing ([Korah et al. 2025](#expansion-refs)). Rapid urban expansion was found to be a major contributor to regional tree cover loss in both Ghana and Nigeria, accounting for 42% of this change area despite occupying only 74% of the study area ([Korah and Wimberly 2026](#expansion-refs)).

- Korah, A., & M. C. Wimberly. 2024a. [Smaller cities have large impacts on West Africa's expanding urban system](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.scs.2024.105381). Sustainable Cities and Society, 106, 105381.
- Korah, A., & M. C. Wimberly. 2024b. [Annual impervious surface data from 2001-2020 for West African countries: Ghana, Togo, Benin, and Nigeria](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-024-03610-8). Scientific Data, 11, 791.
